```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
has_scip <- requireNamespace("scip", quietly = TRUE)
has_osqp <- requireNamespace("osqp", quietly = TRUE)
has_nloptr <- requireNamespace("nloptr", quietly = TRUE)
```

```{r setup}
library(optcompR)
```

optcompR describes an optimization problem once, as variables, expressions,
constraints and an objective, and then classifies it, chooses a capable solver
Large models are built from vectors and sparse matrices, not from loops over
scalars. Expressions store sparse triplets, and products with `Matrix`
objects stay sparse all the way to the solver.

## A sparse LP with 20 000 variables

```{r}
library(Matrix)
set.seed(1)
n <- 20000
k <- 2000
# every row gets at least one entry so the covering problem is feasible
A <- rsparsematrix(k, n, density = 5 / n, rand.x = function(m) runif(m, 0.5, 2)) +
  sparseMatrix(i = 1:k, j = sample(n, k), x = 1, dims = c(k, n))
b <- runif(k, 1, 10)
cost <- runif(n, 1, 3)

m <- opt_model()
x <- opt_variable(m, "x", dim = n, lower = 0)
build <- system.time({
  opt_constraint(m, A %*% x >= b, name = "cover")
  opt_objective(m, sum(cost * x))
})
build[["elapsed"]]
sf <- opt_standard_form(m)
dim(sf$A)
class(sf$A)
r <- opt_solve(m)
opt_status(r)
r$timing
```

One vector constraint gives `k` rows; there is one constraint block, so
`opt_dual(r, "cover")` returns all `k` duals.

```{r}
summary(opt_dual(r, "cover"))
```

## Sparse quadratic objectives

A least squares problem with a sparse design matrix and a ridge penalty:

```{r}
p <- 500
X <- rsparsematrix(2000, p, density = 0.01)
beta <- rnorm(p)
y <- as.vector(X %*% beta) + rnorm(2000, sd = 0.1)
m2 <- opt_model()
bh <- opt_variable(m2, "beta", dim = p)
res <- X %*% bh - y
opt_objective(m2, sum(res^2) + 0.1 * sum(bh^2))
r2 <- opt_solve(m2)
opt_status(r2)
sf2 <- opt_standard_form(m2)
c(nonzeros_in_Q = length(sf2$Q@x), size = nrow(sf2$Q))
```

## Guidelines

* Write `A %*% x` and `sum(w * x)` instead of loops when the data is a matrix.
* Use one constraint block per family of rows; blocks keep names and duals
  organized and are much faster to build than many scalar constraints.
* Parameters avoid rebuilding when only data changes
  (`vignette("parameterized-models")`).
